instructions: Rinse the rice in a strainer under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Cut the ginger into thin coins.
Bring 10 cups of water to a rolling boil in a large pot over high heat. Add the rice, the ginger and 1 tsp of the salt, and stir once.
Turn the heat to low so the water simmers gently. Cover and cook for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes so the rice doesn't stick.
Meanwhile, cut the stems off the shiitake and slice the caps 1/4 inch thick. Thinly slice the scallions.
After the congee has simmered for 15 minutes, stir half of the sliced mushrooms into the pot and keep simmering.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the rest of the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them alone for 3 minutes, until golden underneath. Stir and cook for 2 minutes.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in 2 tsp of the soy sauce.
The congee is ready when the rice has broken down and it's thick and creamy. If it's too thick, stir in a splash of hot water. Stir in the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle the congee into bowls and top with the browned mushrooms, scallions, sesame seeds and a pinch of white pepper. Serve with the chili oil and the remaining 2 tsp soy sauce at the table.

To pack it for lunch, cool the congee and refrigerate it in a covered container for up to 3 days. Reheat it in a pot over low heat with a splash of water, stirring until hot, and add the toppings after.
method_notes: The lead is Che Jorge's vegan congee: 1 cup short-grain rice to 10 cups water with sliced ginger and salt, simmered 30 to 45 minutes. Plateful of Veggies tops its congee with mushrooms browned in a pan with soy sauce, which is used here for half the mushrooms. The other half simmers in the pot as the lead does. The lead keeps 2 to 3 days in the fridge and reheats on the stove with water. The lead has only 13 ratings, so this is a fallback lead. It's over 30 minutes, but it's the kind of lunch you make once and pack.
